questions.question: The official name (in English) of Bangladesh is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**People's Republic of Bangladesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bangladesh** is a country in South Asia that is officially known as the **People's Republic of Bangladesh**.
 
• It is the** world's seventh most populous country**, with almost 163 million people living in an area of either** 148,460 square kilometres or 147,570 square kilometres**, making it one of the **world's most densely inhabited countries**.
 
• Bangladesh shares land boundaries with India to the west, north, and east, as well as Myanmar to the southeast, and the Bay of Bengal to the south.
 
• When Bengali East Pakistan seceded from the union with (West) Pakistan in 1971, the People's Republic of Bangladesh was formed. 
 
• When British India was partitioned along religious, linguistic, and cultural lines in August 1947, the boundaries of contemporary Bangladesh were created.
 
• The western portion of the region became West Bengal, which is today a state in eastern India, and the eastern section became East Pakistan, which was part of the newly founded Pakistan Dominion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bangladesh**__

 
 
• Capital: Dhaka
 
• Currency: Taka
 
• Prime Minister: Sheikh Hasina
 
• President: Abdul Hamid

questions.question: Chenab river of north India originates from the confluence of which of the following two rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandra and Bhaga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Chenab River** is one of the five major rivers in the **Punjab region, flowing through India and Pakistan**.
 
• It is produced by the confluence of two higher Himalayan headwaters**, Chandra and Bhaga**, in the Himachal Pradesh region of Lahaul and Spiti.
 
• Chenab flows through the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir, India, and into the Punjab plains of Pakistan, eventually joining the Indus River.
 
• Under the rules of the Indus Waters Treaty, Pakistan was given the Chenab's waters. Non-consumptive applications, such as power generating, are permitted in India. In Pakistan, the Chenab River is widely used for irrigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The longest of the five tributaries of the** Indus River **that give Punjab its name is the** Sutlej River,** Ancient Greek Zaradros, Sanskrit Shutudri, or Shatadru.
 
• The primary tributaries of the Indus in Kashmir are the **Zaskar, Nubra, Shyok, and Hunza**.
 
• **The Nubra River is a river in Ladakh, India**, that flows through the Nubra Valley.

questions.question: One of the most important descriptions of the city of Vijayanagara in the fifteenth century comes from who among the following diplomats who visited India from Herat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abdur Razzaq Samarqandi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abdur Razzaq Samarqandi, **a diplomat from Herat, provided one of the most famous descriptions of Vijayanagara, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• He was a Persian explorer, historian, and Islamic scholar who travelled to Vijayanagara in the 15th century and wrote about the city's richness, architecture, and inhabitants.
 
• He visited India during the rule of **Deva Raya II **who was the emperor of the Vijayanagar Empire.
 
• The city is now in the state of Karnataka. UNESCO has declared Hampi, which is part of the Vijayanagara ruins, as a world-historic site.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Abd-al-Razzaq Samarqand **was an Islamic scholar and Persian Timurid chronicler. For a while, he was the ambassador of Shah Rukh, the ruler of Persia's Timurid dynasty. In the early 1440s, he travelled to Kozhikode in western India as an ambassador.
 
• Between 1271 and 1295, **Marco Emilio Polo,** a Venetian merchant, explorer, and writer, travelled through Asia along the Silk Road.
 
• **Ibn Battuta** was an Arabized Berber Maghrebi scholar and explorer who travelled extensively throughout Afro-Eurasia, primarily in the Muslim world, more than any other pre-modern explorer.
 
• In the 1740s, **Shaikh Ali Hazin **arrived in north India.

questions.question: On 6th February 2022, which of the following countries became the first to play 1000 one-day internationals (ODI) cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **On February 6, the Indian cricket team** made history by becoming the first team in the world to play** 1,000 One-Day Internationals.**
 
• The team has won **two ODI World Cups and one T20 World Cup**.
 
• In the 1000 ODI matches that India has played thus far, they have 519 victories.
 
• With 958 ODI matches played so far, Australia is in second place.
 
• India becomes the first team to play 1000 One-Day Internationals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **In men's international cricket, **the Indian men's national cricket team, often known as **Team India or the Men in Blue**, represents India.
 
• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) oversees the sport, and it is a Full Member of the International Cricket Council (ICC) with Test, One Day International (ODI), and Twenty20 International (T20I) status.
 
• In the 18th century, British sailors brought cricket to India, and the first cricket club was founded in 1792.
 
• Five major ICC tournaments have been won by India. The team has won the Cricket World Cup twice (1983 and 2011), the ICC T20 World Cup once (2007), and the ICC Champions Trophy twice (2002 and 2013), as well as finishing second in the Cricket World Cup once (2003), the T20 World Cup once (2014).

questions.question: The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (‘NPCSCB’) – ‘Mission Karmayogi’ was launched with the objective of enhancing governance through Civil Service Capacity Building. Which of the following is NOT one of the six pillars of this programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Physical fitness framework**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Civil Service Capacity Building Program (NPCSCB)** is known as **Mission Karmayogi**.
 
• The Indian bureaucracy has undergone a transformation. On **September 2, 2020**, the Union Cabinet officially unveiled it.
 
• The mission's goal is to provide the groundwork for the capacity building of Indian public employees and to improve governance in the country.
 
• The Union Cabinet has started Mission Karmayogi. Between 2020 and 2025, it intends to construct a new national architecture for civil service capacity building at the person, institutional, and process levels.
 
• To carry out this aim, the Companies Act 2013 establishes a special purpose vehicle (SPV) (a non-profit corporation).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB)** aspires to produce a professional, well-trained, and forward-looking civil service that is imbued with a shared awareness of India's developmental goals, national programmes, and objectives.
 
• The NPCSCB's main goal is to improve the citizen-government interaction and make it easier to live and do business. This requires civil servants to develop both functional and behavioural competencies.
 
• The time from 2014 to 2019 was used to achieve the development pre-requisites, and the next five years will be used to meet the aspirations. **Mission Karmayogi **is part of a longer-term reform movement in public HRM and governance that began in 2015.

questions.question: Ugadi Pachadi is a famous dish that is associated with the Ugadi festival of south India. How many different types of ingredients does it contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ugadi Pachadi** is a festive food drink made up of **six different flavours**.
 
• As a result, Ugadi Pachadi has six flavours that correspond to the six emotions of life.
 
• After presenting it to the gods, it is the first dish eaten at the Ugadi festival.
 
• Apart from the health advantages of this festive drink, Ugadi Pachadi also means accepting life in all of its forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **According to the Hindu calendar, Ugadi or Yugadi** is the Hindu New Year's Day, which is observed in the Indian states of **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.**
 
• On the first day of the Hindu lunisolar calendar month of Chaitra, it is celebrated festively in these areas. 
 
• The Pachadi is a popular festive dish that incorporates a wide range of flavours, including sweet, sour, salty, bitter, astringent, and spicy.
 
• It is a symbolic reminder in Telugu and Kannada Hindu traditions that one should expect a wide range of experiences in the approaching new year and make the most of them.

questions.question: While adopting the Constitution of India in 1949, by which Article of the Constitution of India, the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or supplementing the latter Act, EXCEPT the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 was repealed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**395**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 395** repeals the** Indian Independence Act of 1947 and the Government of India Act of 1935**, as well as all amendments and supplements to the latter Act, except the **Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act **of **1949**.
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, abolished the dyarchy established by the Government of India Act, 1919, and established a Federation of India consisting of British India provinces and some or all of the Princely states.
 
• British India was partitioned into India and Pakistan by the Indian Independence Act of 1947.
 
• On July 18, 1947, the Act was signed by** King George VI**, and on August 15, 1947, modern-day Pakistan and India were born.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 394 **states that this article (394) and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392, and 393 shall enter into force immediately, and the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall enter into force on the twenty-sixth day of January 1950, which is referred to as the Constitution's commencement.
 
• **The original Indian Constitution comprised 395 articles and 22 parts** when it was enacted by the Constituent Assembly in 1949.

questions.question: 'Resolved: Uniting Nations in a Divided World' is a memoir of who among the following former UN Secretary Generals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ban Ki-Moon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Former United Nations Secretary-General Ban-Ki-moon's **autobiography is titled** "Resolved: Uniting Nations in a Divided World."**
 
• It includes the author's life experiences and obstacles, as well as details of his time at the United Nations (UN).
 
• He served as the **eighth Secretary-General **of the United Nations from **January 2007 to December 2016**. Ban-Ki-moon goes on to tell how he went from being a "child of war" to becoming a** "man of peace"** in his book** 'Resolved: Uniting Nations in a Divided World,' **published by HarperCollins India.
 
• Former UN Secretary-General Ban-Ki-moon's first diplomatic assignment was in India, where he formed such a strong bond that he still tells the Indian people that half of his "heart belongs in their nation" 50 years later.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Boutros Boutros-Ghali **was an Egyptian politician and diplomat who led the United Nations as its sixth Secretary-General from 1992 to 1996.
 
• **Kofi Atta Annan** was a Ghanaian diplomat who served as the United Nations (UN) seventh Secretary-General from 1997 to 2006.
 
• From 1982 to 1991, Peruvian diplomat and politician **Javier Pérez de Cuéllar** served as the United Nations' fifth Secretary-General.

questions.question: The Advocate General of each state of India is appointed by:

options.text: the Chief Minister of the State

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the Governor of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A state government's **advocate general** is a legal advisor. The post was formed by the Indian Constitution (see **Article 165**) and is equivalent to the position of **Attorney General for India at the federal level**.
 
• **The Advocate General **is appointed by the Governor of each state and must be eligible to serve as a High Court judge.
 
• The Attorney General of India is governed by** Article 76** of the Indian Constitution, whereas the Advocate General of India is governed by **Article 165**.
 
• Because the former is the chief law officer of the state and the latter is the highest law officer of India, the offices of Advocate General of State and Attorney General of India are interchangeable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indian President **selects **Governors **for each state by a warrant signed and sealed by him. Each state's governor is appointed by the federal government.
 
• The Governor's post has no set term because he serves at the pleasure of the President. The President has the power to remove the Governor, and the grounds for his removal are not specified in the constitution.
 
• The President may also transfer the Governor from one state to another. He can also be reappointed.

questions.question: In 1943, some of the younger leaders in which district of Maharashtra set up a parallel government (Prati Sarkar), with volunteer corps (Seba dals) and village units (Tufan dals )?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Satara Parallel Government **in Maharashtra, which fought British control from** August 1943 to May 1946,** was a legendary chapter in India's historic freedom war.
 
• It, like the parallel administrations in Bengal's Midnapore, Bihar's Bhagalpur, Uttar Pradesh's Ballia, and Odisha's Basudevpur, was an armed outgrowth of the 1942 Quit India movement.
 
• **'Kratisimha' Nana Patil (1900-1976),** the leader of the Satara Parallel administration, later joined the Communist Party and was elected to the Lok Sabha on the CPI platform from Satara in 1957 and Beed in 1967.
 
• **The Prati Sarkar (Parallel Government) **movement was a guerilla movement that operated in over 150 villages with widespread peasant backing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satara** is a city in Maharashtra, located near the confluence of the Krishna River and its tributary, the Venna.
 
• The city was founded in the 16th century and served as the capital of the Maratha Empire's Chhatrapati, Shahu I.

questions.question: In which of the following countries did the former prime minister Lal Bahadur Shastri die?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uzbekistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **On the 11th of January 1966, Lal Bahadur Shastri **died in **Tashkent, Uzbekistan** (then Soviet Union), one day after signing a peace accord ending the 1965 Indo-Pakistan War.
 
• He was hailed as a national hero, and the Vijay Ghat memorial was named for him. Following Shastri's death, Gulzarilal Nanda was re-elected as acting prime minister until Indira Gandhi was voted over Morarji Desai by the Congress Parliamentary Party to officially succeed him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lal Bahadur Shastri **was a statesman from India who served as the country's second prime minister.
 
• He supported the Amul milk cooperative in Anand, Gujarat, and established the Countrywide Dairy Development Board to promote the White Revolution, a national drive to improve milk production and supply.
 
• Shastri championed the Green Revolution in India in 1965, highlighting the need to increase India's food production.
 
• Food grain production increased as a result, particularly in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• During the 1965 Indo-Pakistan War, he was the country's leader.
 
• During the conflict, his slogan** "Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan" **became immensely famous.

questions.question: Who among the following got Padma Vibhushan Award 2022 under the civil service category?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bipin Rawat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **General Bipin Rawat, India's first Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)**, was posthumously awarded t**he Padma Vibhushan**.
 
• He died in a helicopter mishap in December 2021. On behalf of the CDS, his daughters Kritika and Tarini accepted the honour.
 
• President Ram Nath Kovind presented the prize to the daughters. In December of last year, General Bipin Rawat, India's first Chief of Defence Staff, died in a helicopter crash.
 
• The helicopter disaster also claimed the lives of General Rawat's wife, Madhulika Rawat, and 12 other defence personnel.
 
• Padma Awards, which are among the country's highest civilian honours, are divided into three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• These honours are bestowed by the** President of India** at ceremonial occasions held at Rashtrapati Bhavan every year around March/April.
 
• The President has approved the conferral of 128 Padma Awards this year, including two pair cases (in a duo case, the Award is counted as one). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Rajiv Mehrishi, the former Comptroller and Auditor General of India**, was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** award in the category of Civil Services at the Rashtrapati Bhawan.
 
• In the field of Trade and Industry, **Natrajan Chandrasekaran** earned the third highest civilian honour, the **Padma Bhushan**.

questions.question: Who among the following received Padma Bhushan 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Victor Banerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Victor Banerjee,** a three-time National Award winner, was given the** Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award,** in the field of art by the Indian government in 2022.
 
• At Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President also handed out four Padma Vibhushans and 107 Padma Shri.
 
• In David Lean's film **"A Passage to India"**, Banerjee played Dr. Aziz Ahmed, bringing him to the notice of western audiences.
 
• In 1986, he was nominated for a BAFTA award for the part, which he won as well as the Evening Standard British Film Award and the NBR Award (National Board Review, USA). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **President Ram Nath Kovind** honoured **Konsam Ibomcha Singh**, a traditional Laiphadibi doll maker from Manipur, with the Padma Shri Award for Arts.
 
• **Lourembam Bino Devi** is a practitioner and popularizer of Manipur's appliqué craft, known as Leeba in Meitei.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Padma Bhushan** is the Republic of India's third-highest civilian award, after the Bharat Ratna and Padma Vibhushan, and before the Padma Shri.
 
• The award, which was established on January 2, 1954, recognizes "distinguished service of a high order...without difference of race, occupation, status, or sex."
 
• The award criteria include "service in any discipline, including service performed by Government workers," such as doctors and scientists, but exclude individuals who work for government-owned businesses.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states were the remains of the ancient Vikramshila University discovered?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vikramshila** is an ancient site located 40 km away from the Bhagalpur city of Bihar.
 
• The small town is famous for housing **Vikramshila University**, which was built under the guidance of **Dharmapala, a Pala King of the 8th century AD**.
 
• Situated on top of the hills along the banks of the river Ganges, the university became a learning centre of Tantric Buddhism.
 
• Over the years, Vikramshila became one of the most popular Buddhist destinations in India and a major tourist spot in Bihar. 
 
• It prospered for about four centuries before it was destroyed by **Bakhtiyar Khilji **along with the other major centres of Buddhism in India **around** **1193**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **During the Pala Empire, Vikramashila**, along with Nalanda and Odantapuri, was one of India's three most prominent Buddhist monasteries.
 
• In response to a perceived decrease in the quality of study at Nalanda, the Pala ruler Dharmapala (783–820 AD) founded Vikramashila.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Aves (birds) class of animals?

options.text: The skin is dry without glands except the oil gland at the base of the tail.
The hind limbs are modified into wings.
The presence of feathers and most of them can fly except flightless birds.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The hind limbs are modified into wings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Forelimbs and hindlimbs **are found on birds. The forelimbs are transformed into wings.
 
• Scales cover the hindlimbs, which are specialised for walking, jumping, and grasping tree branches. Birds have a **warm-blooded nature**.
 
• **Aves** are a group of endothermic animals that include birds.
 
• These animals belong to the Chordata phylum and have characteristics such as toothless jaws with a beak, hard-shelled eggs, and so on.
 
• In the terrestrial animal realm, there are an estimated 9000 Aves species. This species' most prominent attribute is its ability to fly.
 
• Their skeletal structure, which is made up of strong but hollow bones, allows them to fly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The fact that they are bipedal feathered animals is one of the most noticeable traits of the Aves class.
 
• Birds' forelimbs have evolved into wings that allow them to fly.
 
• Their back limbs have evolved into legs that aid them in swimming, walking, and other activities. Birds' legs often have four toes.
 
• Two or three toes, on the other hand, are rarely noticeable.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) scheme launched by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2009**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA)** is a centrally funded scheme run by **India's Ministry of Human Resource Development **to improve secondary education in public schools across the country.
 
• It was first released in March of **2009**. The scheme's implementation began in 2009-2010 with the goal of creating circumstances for efficient growth, development, and equity for all.
 
• Multidimensional research, technical consulting, numerous implementations, and financial support are all part of the plan.
 
• **The main goals were to improve secondary education quality and to increase total enrollment from 52 percent in 2005–2006 to 75 percent in five years, from 2009 to 2014.**
 
• Its goal was to provide universal education to all children aged 15 to 16. The central ministry funds are channelled through state governments, which set up their own implementation organisations.

questions.question: Different species of Plasmodium (a tiny protozoan) are responsible for different types of malaria, of these, malignant malaria which is the most serious is caused by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**plasmodium falciparum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Different species of Plasmodium (a tiny protozoan) **are responsible for different types of malaria, of these, malignant malaria which is the most serious is caused by** plasmodium falciparum**.
 
• **Plasmodia **are a type of protozoa. Humans are usually infected with Plasmodium falciparum, Plasmodium vivax, Plasmodium malariae, and Plasmodium ovale. **P falciparum **is the most serious of the three.
 
• **Plasmodium falciparum **is a human unicellular protozoan parasite that causes malaria. It is the **deadliest Plasmodium species.**
 
• The parasite is spread via the bite of a female Anopheles mosquito, which produces falciparum malaria, the most deadly form of the disease.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Human malaria is caused by **Plasmodium Malariae****, a parasitic protozoan.**
 
• **Plasmodium vivax** is a human pathogen and a protozoal parasite. This parasitic infection is the most common and widespread cause of recurrent malaria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malaria** is a parasitic disease spread by mosquitoes. Humans are infected with the parasite after being bitten by infected mosquitoes.
 
• Malaria makes people feel very sick, with a high fever and shivering chills.
 
• Malaria is still frequent in tropical and subtropical nations, despite its rarity in temperate settings.

questions.question: What is the term used for a non-living part of an ecosystem that shapes its environment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abiotic factor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abiotic factors** are non-living components of an ecosystem that influence its surroundings.
 
• Temperature, light, and water are examples of variables in a terrestrial environment.
 
• Abiotic elements in a marine ecosystem include salinity and ocean currents.
 
• A unique ecosystem is created by the interaction of abiotic and biotic factors.
 
• The ecosystem is a natural functional unit in which living species interact with one another as well as with the physical surroundings.
 
• There are two parts to the ecosystem: (The environment is shaped by these two variables.)

 
• **Biotic factor**
 
• **Abiotic factor**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• A living entity that shapes its surroundings is referred to as a** biotic factor**.
 
• A dimensionless scale factor governs the universe's relative expansion. This is a significant parameter in the Friedmann equations, often known as the** cosmic scale factor** or the Robertson Walker scale factor.
 
• **Amniotic fluid **embolism is a rare but life-threatening illness that happens when amniotic fluid (the fluid that surrounds a baby in the uterus during pregnancy) or foetal material (such as foetal cells) enters the mother's bloodstream.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam dance emotes a play through dancing and singing where the song is customarily in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipravala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mohiniattam** stands apart from all other Indian dance genres because of its captivating grace.
 
• Mohiniattam is only a couple of centuries old in its current shape. Before reaching its current state, the dance form underwent stylistic transformations.
 
• Traditions never remain static; they change over time as a result of shifting aesthetic and social tastes. Female artists do Mohiniattam, a solo performance.
 
• The song is generally in **Manipravala**, which is a **blend of Sanskrit and Malayalam**, and the dance emotes a play through dancing and singing. The recitation is also performed in Carnatic music style, either by the dancer or by the vocalist. 
 
• **Manipravalami **is a South Indian macaronic language documented in some texts. It is a hybrid language that blends Sanskrit vocabulary with Tamil morpho-syntax and is commonly written in the Grantha script.
 
• However, the Sanskrit text Lilatilakam, written in the 14th century, claims that Manipravalam is a hybrid of Tamil and Sanskrit.
